ia-board-chair.summary: Your County Supervisor card names the supervisors, and in 35 of Iowa's 99 counties it now also says which one chairs the board. In the other 64 it cannot: nothing published there pairs a chair with a name.
ia-board-chair.why: No statewide publisher records the chair at all, so it has to come from each county's own board page — and most either name no chair, refuse this app outright, or word it so loosely that no reading of it is safe enough to ship.
ia-board-chair.wanted: A county board page that names its chair beside the member, or a statewide list carrying a chair column — the supervisors' own association directory already names every member and would need only that one field.

ia-municipal-officeholders.summary: The City card names your city and nothing else — not your mayor, not your council, not your clerk. That is true in 833 of Iowa's 939 cities; in the other 106 either the city or its county publishes them.
ia-municipal-officeholders.why: No one publishes Iowa's city officeholders in one place, and the cities do not publish alike: two in five have no website at all. Nine counties do publish every city inside them, which is where most of the named ones come from.
ia-municipal-officeholders.wanted: More counties publishing their cities' officials the way nine already do, or a city's own council page. Best of all, one statewide list of Iowa's city clerks — the shape Wisconsin's Elections Commission supplies for its municipalities.

ia-polling-places.summary: Your precinct card names your precinct and cannot tell you where to vote in it. The state does publish every polling place in Iowa — but nothing published says which precinct each one serves.
ia-polling-places.why: The two things needed exist in different files. Everything that says which precinct a place serves is two years old; the current list dropped that column, so nothing joins it to a precinct without going through a stale map.
ia-polling-places.wanted: The precinct name carried alongside each polling place in the current file, as the previous edition carried it — one column, and the card could name your polling place. Failing that, any published pairing of precinct to place.

johnson-county-supervisor-districts.summary: Johnson County's supervisor card names the county and says its districts are pending — it cannot yet tell you which of the five you live in.
johnson-county-supervisor-districts.why: The county adopted five districts for the November 2026 election but publishes them only as a printed map, and the statewide layer this app reads still carries the county under its older at-large form.
johnson-county-supervisor-districts.wanted: A map of the five districts the county can share as data, or a link to one — the way Black Hawk County publishes its own.

jones-county-supervisor.summary: Jones County carries no supervisor-district card at all — the county is entirely absent from the state's own statewide aggregate.
jones-county-supervisor.why: The Iowa Legislature's own CountySupervisorDistricts layer is this app's only statewide source, and Jones County has zero rows in it — measured both by name and by its own FIPS code (105), not a naming mismatch.
jones-county-supervisor.wanted: The county's own GIS file for the districts its own map already shows, or the state adding Jones to its statewide aggregate. Not an extraction from that published map — it carries no usable shapes, which was measured rather than assumed.

marion-council-roster.summary: Marion elects its council by ward, and its ward boundaries are already measured and ready — but no ward card ships, because nothing here can name the four members who hold those seats.
marion-council-roster.why: The city's own website refuses this app's requests outright, and every other publisher checked maps its wards without naming its council: the county draws the boundaries, and no directory carries the people.
marion-council-roster.wanted: A council page this app can reach, or the four ward members' names with the ward each holds — the boundary is already built and waiting on exactly that.
